previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of recurrent pancreatitis was admitted due to a relapse of severe right epigastric pain shortly after discharge from a prior hospitalization. She was initially kept NPO and managed with IV fluids and a hydromorphone PCA for pain control. Imaging with MRCP showed chronic changes consistent with prior pancreatitis but no acute complications. A PICC line was placed for fluid and medication access, later replaced due to poor flow. Parenteral nutrition was initiated to support nutritional recovery. Her pain improved, allowing transition to oral medications and gradual advancement of diet. Diarrhea was attributed to a new bowel regimen, with negative C. difficile testing. She was discharged home in improved condition with a plan for oral pain management, GI follow-up, and continuation of psychiatric medications.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted with a flare of your chronic pancreatitis. You 
were placed on bowel rest and given TPN through the IV for 
nutrition. You were given hydromorphone for pain control.  You 
had an endoscopic ultrasound of your pancreas which showed no 
evidence of masses.  
.
An ultrasound of your arm was performed near the sight of your 
picc line and showed a non-occlusive clot around the picc line, 
and the picc line was subsequently switched to your other arm.  
You will continue to receive TPN through the picc line once you 
are discharged, and the TPN will be cycled at 12 hours/day to 
allow you some flexibility.  The visiting nurse service will 
assist you in the care of your picc line and TPN.
.
Please DISCONTINUE taking your Premarin, since estrogens have 
been implicated in the formation of blood clots.  At your next 
appointment with your PCP, you should plan on discussing the 
continued need for taking estrogens with him.  He will recommend 
whether or not you should continue on Premarin.  
.

You should call your PCP or go to the emergency room if you have 
fevers over 102, chills, worsening abdominal pain, severe nausea 
or vomiting, black or tarry stools or any other symptoms which 
are concerning to you.

radiology_notes.text:
AP CHEST ON ___, 11:24 A.M.

HISTORY:  Left PIC.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Left PIC catheter has been withdrawn minimally back to the low SVC.  Lungs
clear.  Heart size normal.  No pleural abnormality or evidence of central
adenopathy.  Findings discussed with the IV nurse earlier in the day.

INDICATION:  Erythema and edema near PICC line.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and Doppler sonograms of the left internal jugular,
subclavian, axillary, brachial, basilic, and cephalic veins were performed.
Flow is seen throughout the vessels; however, echogenic material is seen
adjacent to the PICC line in the basilic, especially near the elbow.  Findings
are suggestive of a non-occlusive thrombus.

IMPRESSION:  Findings suggesting non-occlusive thrombus in the basilic vein
surrounding the PICC line. Findings discussed with Dr. ___ on ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  ___ female with chronic pancreatitis.  In need of
PICC line for TPN.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___.  Attending radiologist, Dr.
___, was present and supervised the entire procedure.

PROCEDURE/FINDINGS:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right
basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set.  Hard copies of the ultrasound images were obtained before
and immediately after establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was
then placed over a guide wire and a double-lumen PIC line measuring 34 cm in
length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in
SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.  The peel-away sheath and guide wire were
then removed.  The catheter was secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile
dressing applied.  The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no
immediate complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopic-guided double-lumen
PICC line placement via the right basilic vein approach.  Final internal
length is 34 cm with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready to use.
